authority.duplicates: Duplicate paths, duplicate header, malformed digest/path or embedded control characters => ERROR.
authority.format: First line exactly SLP-SUDOERS-REVIEWED-POLICY-V1; each following line is lowercase sha256<TAB>absolute_path. Blank/comment lines are not allowed.
authority.meaning: Each listed digest approves the exact bytes of one active sudoers policy file; the set of listed paths must exactly equal the active visudo closure.

compliance.error: ERROR: authority invalid/unavailable; visudo unavailable/fails; closure output ambiguous; active member is symlink/nonregular/unreadable; hashing/tool observation fails.
compliance.fail: VALUE/FAIL: determinate active closure differs from reviewed authority by pathset or exact file bytes.
compliance.pass: VALUE/PASS: visudo valid; closure determinate; every active file exact-byte digest equals reviewed authority and pathsets are identical.

runtime.binary: Policy bytes are not line-normalized before hashing; authority is raw-byte validated before line parsing.
runtime.closure: Only exact `PATH: parsed OK` lines from successful visudo output are admitted. Unexpected output, duplicate paths, relative paths, symlink/nonregular/unreadable policy files => ERROR.
runtime.comparison: For every active file compute SHA-256 of exact bytes. Exact pathset+digest equality to authority => PASS; any missing/extra path or digest drift => VALUE/FAIL.
runtime.syntax: LC_ALL=C /usr/sbin/visudo -c -f /etc/sudoers must succeed; validation is mandatory but not sufficient.

source_interpretation.authority: The reviewed local decision is represented by an explicit product authority manifest; this is a product mechanism, not a separate FSTEC requirement.
source_interpretation.closure: The policy tree is the main /etc/sudoers plus every file actually parsed by visudo through include/includedir processing.
source_interpretation.no_discovery: Approved users/commands are not inferred from %sudo, %wheel, SUDO_USER, donor defaults or reference VMs.
source_interpretation.review: Source requires restricting who may use sudo and which commands may be run by reviewing /etc/sudoers; it does not define a universal user/command set.

source_requirement: 2.2.2. Ограничить список пользователей, которым разрешено использовать команду sudo и разрешенных к выполнению через sudo команд путём пересмотра файла /etc/sudoers.

vm_evidence.facts: Across all seven /etc/sudoers was regular root:root mode 0440, @includedir /etc/sudoers.d was present and full visudo validation returned RC=0; Ubuntu 26 exposed sudo/visudo through alternatives symlinks.
vm_evidence.matrix: 7/7 integrity-verified Ubuntu22 FULL; Ubuntu24 MINIMIZED/FULL; Ubuntu26 MINIMIZED/FULL; Debian12 SERVER; Debian13 GNOME.
vm_evidence.scope: Evidence validates discovery assumptions only; it does not define approved local sudo policy and does not expand current product target.
